recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a portrait-first mobile dress-up game where the player styles a plushie-soft office main character in a cozy satirical breakroom closet. Preserve the mechanics: start overlay, category tabs, prev/next wraparound cycling, canvas avatar preview, sound toggle, and lock-look celebration. Do not add score, hazards, timers, or loss states. Present the world with warm paper UI, plants, sticky notes, desk lamp lighting, fairycore softness, meme copy, and fashion/makeover hooks. Use one-thumb controls in a readable bottom sheet and keep all core code browser-native.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: mobile portrait dress-up / avatar customization toy.
- objective: choose customization categories, cycle options, preview the canvas avatar, and lock the final look.
- input model: tap category tabs, tap previous/next arrows, tap sound toggle, tap lock-look, tap start overlay.
- core loop: start session -> select category -> wrap through available variants -> redraw avatar immediately -> optionally lock look for celebratory feedback.
- fail/friction state: no game-over; only harmless audio failures or cosmetic feedback states. Wraparound means options never block.

## Protected mechanics
- Single canonical portrait customizer surface.
- Start overlay gates first user gesture and audio setup.
- Horizontal category tabs select the active customization lane.
- Previous/next buttons wrap cyclically through each lane's finite option list.
- Canvas avatar updates immediately from shared state.
- Lock Look gives temporary confirmation without changing scoring, progression, or input semantics.
- Sound toggle is user-gesture-safe and non-blocking.

## Remixed target
Deskcore Dress Up: No Thoughts Makeover preserves the dress-up customizer loop while reframing the avatar as a plushie-aesthetic office main character doing a cozy weekend makeover in a fairycore breakroom. The Office-inspired satire appears through HR/sticky-note copy, desk props, meeting jokes, and lock-look feedback, while the visual world uses Ghibli-adjacent softness, plants, warm paper, plush rounded forms, and one-thumb mobile controls.
